author: nflaig
content: <@755590043632140352> just for my understanding, so your main concern isn't really the amount of bids, but rather that certain bids (even just a single one) can force expensive state regen in clients and act as a dos? if that's the case then I think best it to either just use head state (but you still need to dial bid slot) or just do this on a best effort basis and just drop the bids you cannot cheaply verify, not sure that warrants a note in the spec

author: potuz
content: No, my main concern is P2P propagation itself. By allowing to broadcast a bid that is not compatible with my view of the chain I'm allowing for arbitrary objects to propagate that are useless. If the parent block has 100% of the vote and I send a bid on top of grandparent with a ridiculously high value I'm guaranteed to reach every node in the chain. I can do this at no cost since my bid is unincludable. I believe this is a bad design for the P2P stack.  It's akin to sending a block based on 32 slots ago, just that I don't lose anything and I can do it every slot

author: potuz
content: I believe most cases you want to cover, if not all, are already covered by the head view. We will have bids for full and empty being propagated when the Payload is late

author: nflaig
content: `get_head` can be different than what the proposer will build on as proposers evaluate differently already in fulu with `get_proposer_head` and especially in gloas since we have `should_build_on_full`, so `get_head` of attesters/normal nodes can be `FULL` while proposer can select `EMPTY`

author: potuz
content: yeah, this is the spirit. I am less concerned with proposer boost reorgs, but I agree with Nico that the resolver should have in mind should_build_on_full perhaps, the choice between full or empty should be allowed to propagate. In theory if everyone got the payload early, only full should propagate, if everyone got it late, only empty should propagate, but if it was mixed then some will and some wont
